answer: To resist sybil attacks, a new agent must dock at a limited-throughput admission jetty and lock a slashable bond before receiving any identity. Reviewers then consult a public atlas of prior keys, stake graphs, and cluster fingerprints to detect clone farms. Only after that check does a credential forge mint the agent; if later evidence shows coordinated sockpuppets, the bond is burned and the graph is marked, making mass registration expensive in both capital and social proof.
